title: Multi-tenant metrics dropout during router failover; trace reassembly and dashboard repopulation
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: Several Hosted and Dedicated tenants reported missing dashboard tiles and gaps in traces after a cascading router failover on 2026-03-09. Symptoms included: per-tenant time series disappearing for 2-7 minutes, live panels showing 'no data', and traces present in raw span storage but unable to stitch to dashboards or SLO alerts. This ticket coordinates immediate customer escalations, the hotfix deployment, and a post-incident remediation plan.

Impact: High — multiple paying customers on hosted and a Dedicated tenant experienced alerts firing and observed blank dashboard tiles during the recovery window. Customers contacted support and escalations were opened.

Reproduction notes: In our staging environment, triggering an aggressive router kill sequence (simulate connection churn + concurrent shard reassigns) reproduces: (1) metric envelopes routed to temporary ingest buckets with TTL=1h instead of tenant buckets, (2) index pointers in the metrics index being advanced while shard ownership transitions, and (3) span parent_id headers truncated on a subset of HTTP keepalive connections leading to disconnected traces.

Root cause (interim findings): A combination of three interacting faults: 
1) The rebalancer's shard-transfer window began relying on a new ephemeral-bucket path during churn; when churn overlapped with a backlog flush, some metric batches were written to ephemeral buckets that are excluded from the live-query path.
2) The metrics index advance logic (recent change in runtime-1.25) assumed idempotent batch ordering; during reassign it skipped a commit point and left 'last-committed' pointers ahead of written data, so live-queries returned 'no data' for that window.
3) On the tracing side, an optimisation to header compression + keepalive reuse (edge proxy change from 2026-02) occasionally truncated the tracestate/parent header when the connection was reused mid-write, breaking parent-child linkage for spans.

Immediate mitigations applied (what was executed): 
- Rolled back runtime-1.25 commit containing metrics index change (hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6784) to stop pointer advancement.
- Reverted ephemeral-bucket write switch in rebalancer; re-enabled writing to guaranteed tenant ingest buckets.
- Deployed tracing header fix as a staged rollout to 10% infra to add defensive header length checks and copy-on-write for header buffers (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/221).
- Backfilled missing metric batches from ephemeral buckets to tenant buckets using ad-hoc rehydration job (runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/ephemeral-rehydrate). Job ID: rehydrate-20260310-01.

Proposed permanent fixes and timeline: 
1) Rebalancer: add transactional handoff and write-confirmation step before retiring source shard (owner: Lina Gomez, ETA: 2026-03-21).
2) Metrics index: implement a commit-log compact-and-verify pass at shard-ownership transfer to ensure last-committed pointers match persisted batch sequence (owner: Marcus Holt, ETA: 2026-03-18).
3) Tracing: strengthen header validation and add test harness for connection reuse edge cases; add trace-stitcher repair tool to re-link orphan spans using timing/trace IDs (owner: Daniel Kim, ETA: 2026-03-20).
4) Dashboard resilience: modify live-panel queries to fall back to a short historical window with progressive backfill if no data is returned and surface 'recovering' banner to customers (owner: Product/Console: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-03-30).

Customer communications: Support drafted a status update for impacted tenants pointing to mitigation steps and estimated restoration timeline. Tech lead on escalation calls: Asha Patel. Customer follow-ups scheduled for 2026-03-15.

Acceptance criteria for Done: 
- No further metric dropouts under synthetic router failover scenario in staging.
- Backfill job validated and dashboards repopulated for sample tenants.
- Rollout of tracing fix confirmed by end-to-end trace stitching in 95th percentile test.
- Postmortem completed and shared with customers and SRE rotation.

Related artifacts:
- Hotfix PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/6784, https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/221
- Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/ephemeral-rehydrate
- Quick dashboard snapshot: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/tenant-sample/recovery-2026-03-10

Longer term follow-ups (post-incident):
- Introduce canary for rebalancer changes with synthetic tenant micro-loads.
- Add metric integrity checks on ingest (per-tenant sequence checks).
- Scheduled glue job to periodically reconcile ephemeral buckets to tenant buckets for first 72 hours after any rebalancer deployment.

This ticket will track the engineering fixes and be linked to customer escalation cases in Support (SUP-2143, SUP-2148).
